quote: OpenClaw is a legitimately capable open-source autonomous agent framework with real coding strengths, an impressive community ecosystem, and some security considerations that developers absolutely need to understand before running it anywhere that matters.
author: TheModernBlog Team
notes: TheModernBlog hands-on weeks-of-use review: capable but security caveats.

quote: In January 2026, security researchers disclosed CVE-2026-25253, a cross-site WebSocket hijacking vulnerability rated CVSS 8.8. The vulnerability meant that any website could steal an auth token and achieve remote code execution on the host machine through a single malicious link. One click and an attacker had full access to whatever the OpenClaw Gateway could access. The vulnerability was patched in version 2026.1.29, but security firm Censys found over 21,000 OpenClaw instances exposed to the public internet at the time of disclosure, many running over plain HTTP.
author: TheModernBlog Team
notes: CVE-2026-25253 WebSocket hijack; 21k exposed instances at disclosure.

quote: In February 2026, the ClawHavoc supply chain attack resulted in 341 malicious skills being uploaded to ClawHub, compromising over 9,000 installations with credential-stealing malware. A Cisco security team audit also found a skill that had been gamed to the top of the repository and contained hidden malicious behavior.
author: TheModernBlog Team
notes: ClawHavoc: 341 malicious ClawHub skills, 9k+ installs compromised.

quote: According to source [3], Gartner warned of "unacceptable cybersecurity risk," Cisco's AI security research team flagged it as a cautionary example, the Belgian Cybersecurity Centre issued an immediate-patch advisory, and CrowdStrike found deployed instances running over unencrypted HTTP.
author: Ivan Protsko
notes: unsubbed.co synthesis of enterprise security firm warnings.

quote: Hermes is the agent I switched to after I found OpenClaw too unreliable. I run it through Telegram on a Mac Mini inside my house.
author: Peter Yang
notes: Creator Economy: left OpenClaw for Hermes due to unreliability.

quote: Orchestration via OpenClaw first, and Hermes later. ... For me, this migration had already started slowly, with experiments here and there, but got a decisive acceleration when I tried Grok Bot this month.
author: Luca Rossi
notes: Refactoring.fm path: OpenClaw → Hermes → Grok Bot for orchestration.

quote: if you are on a stable 2026.9.1 or 2026.9.2 build, hold off for a few days. … Do not rush to 2026.9.4 the day it ships. … Report #144788 is a critical regression naming 9.4 directly: post-agent-end memory generation fails for affected plugin setups that worked on 9.1 through 9.3. Report #144809 loses entire generated replies on long claude-cli turns.
author: Marcus Li

quote: an update fails, the system rolls back to the 2026.9.2 runtime, but the Skill Workshop data has already moved forward to the new ownership model. The old runtime then fails Doctor because it expects workspace_dir while the database now has owner_agent_id. You end up on 9.2 with 9.3-shaped data, which is the worst of both worlds.
author: Marcus Li

quote: OpenClaw 2.0 is best understood as a self-hosted AI agent gateway, not as another large language model. … promising for developers, automation-heavy teams, and users who want an open, local-first agent system. It is less suitable for people who simply want a polished one-click chatbot.
author: Daniel Brooks
notes: AirMore OpenClaw 2.0 review: gateway framing + setup tradeoff.

quote: OpenClaw is the open-source personal assistant you run yourself. It lives in WhatsApp, iMessage, Telegram, Slack, Signal — the chats you already have — and talks to whatever model you plug in. Best if you want control and will own the setup. Not a consumer app.
author: Neeraj Nathany
notes: Faraday field map: OpenClaw as self-host control pick.

quote: I've been running OpenClaw as my main personal agent setup for about 13 weeks now. It runs on a Raspberry Pi, talks to me through Telegram, manages memory, crons, subagents, research workflows, external APIs, scheduled tasks and general personal automation. … The short version: OpenClaw is powerful enough that I now treat it as infrastructure. It is also still rough enough that you need patience, logs, backups and a willingness to debug weird edge cases.
author: u/LobsterWeary2675
notes: r/openclaw 13-week daily-driver recap (missed by prior scans); infrastructure not consumer polish.

quote: After roughly 3 month, I would not remove OpenClaw from my setup. It has crossed the line from experiment to daily infrastructure. But I also would not call it effortless. It is powerful, sharp and occasionally annoying. … If you expect "install it and it just runs my life", you will be disappointed. If you are willing to treat it like infrastructure, it can become extremely useful.
author: u/LobsterWeary2675
notes: Same 13-week post: keep it as daily infra; not effortless consumer PA.

quote: Trail of Bits submitted 27 private repository advisories and 3 standalone hardening pull requests. Of the advisory reports, 24 described severity-rated vulnerabilities. 23 were classified as confirmed vulnerabilities… Those 24 reports were rated 0 Critical, 2 High, 16 Medium, and 6 Low. … Every actionable issue has been repaired, and all 3 standalone hardening PRs were merged.
author: Josh Avant
notes: Sep 21 Patch the Planet / Trail of Bits audit recap; fixes shipped in 2026.8.1 / 2026.7.33 LTS.

quote: If memory access was enabled when a run began and the operator disabled it midway through, that run could continue reading memory until it ended. The fix was to make tools check the current setting whenever they act.
author: Josh Avant
notes: Audit lesson: mid-run permission changes must re-check; fixed.

quote: I reached the Control UI and connected OpenAI, but my first live memory task returned an authentication error after about 25 seconds. Even after I completed the OpenAI sign-in, the agent still failed before producing a reply. … I'd recommend it if you have recurring jobs for an assistant and don't mind troubleshooting. It isn't my first pick if you want a simple AI assistant that works straight away.
author: Bhavyadeep
notes: Sep 8 Windows retest: install OK, live memory task still fails post-OAuth. Missed by prior scans.
